newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares dive after S&P downgrading.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares dive after S&P downgrading.

text.p: Turkish shares fell sharply in heavy selling on Monday and the lira weakened sharply against the dollar in reaction to Standard & Poor's downgrading of Turkey's long-term foreign currency debt rating, dealers said.
They said the markets were awaiting a downgrading since early last week, so the news of Friday's move by S&P did not affect sentiment too badly.

"The stock market fell sharply, but was not shocked by the news because many players had discounted the expectation last week that the S&P would downgrade Turkey's rating," said Ugur Under from Boyut securities.

The IMKB-100 plunged 5.5 percent to a low of 84,446 at the opening and later recovered slightly on reaction buys. It stood at 86,103.93 in the second half of the morning session, down 3,232.93 points, or 3.62 percent from Friday.
The lira eased to 105,400 against the dollar on the interbank, from Friday's 104,160 close due to the rating downgrade and a higher dollar/mark parity in world markets.

The S&P cut Turkey's long-term foreign currency rating to "single B" from "single B-plus" and affirmed its "single-B" short-term foreign currency debt rating on Friday and said the outlook on Turkey's long-term foreign currency rating was stable.
"A downgrading was expected, so the markets remained calm although the dollar opened sharply higher and Treasury-bill yields rose," said a private banker.
Yields on the bond market rose by between two and three points across the board in thin trade.
Bankers expect the markets to remain calm due to strong central bank currency reserves and financial institutions' experiences from 1994 financial crises when they posted sharp losses.
